DTCC Launches Securities Tokenization Service, Initially Supporting 34 Securities DTCC’s website shows that its Tokenization Service is now live, initially supporting 34 securities, including selected large-cap Russell 1000 constituents, ETFs and U.S. Treasuries. Tokens are backed 1:1 by underlying securities held in custody by the Depository Trust Company (DTC), carry the same legal and ownership rights, and support round-the-clock onchain transfers between DTC-registered wallets. The service initially supports Canton Network and DTCC’s Besu-based private network, with Stellar and Circle’s Arc expected to join in 2027. — link

Bank of Canada Raises Policy Rate by 25 Basis Points to 2.5% in First Hike in Three Years The Bank of Canada on October 28, 2026, raised its target for the overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%, the first increase since July 2023. The Bank Rate is now 2.75% and the deposit rate is 2.45%. The move aims to reduce the risk that persistently high energy prices spread to the prices of other goods and services. Governing Council said the policy rate may need to rise further, but it will proceed carefully given the uncertainties. — link

Y Combinator Highlights Stablecoins, AI Fundraising, Tokenization and Agent Infrastructure as Key Crypto Startup Opportunities Y Combinator (YC) outlined its crypto startup priorities for the next six months in its October 2026 Crypto Request for Startups, highlighting blockchain-based AI fundraising, new USD and non-USD stablecoins, stablecoin-powered neobanks, real-world asset tokenization, new trading platforms, and AI agent trading and API infrastructure. YC noted that institutional adoption had driven crypto growth over the past year, with demand shifting from speculation toward financial use cases such as hedging and cross-border payments. It expects more assets to be tokenized, new on-chain financial instruments to emerge, and AI agents to become major participants in financial markets. — link

Bloomberg: Over $170M in Unusual Hyperliquid Oil Perp Orders Raise Spoofing Suspicions According to Bloomberg, market surveillance firm Solidus Labs identified over $170 million in unusual orders placed through two Hyperliquid accounts between March 8 and 10, amid sharp oil price swings linked to the Iran war. The activity raised concerns about potential spoofing in oil perpetual futures markets. The trader repeatedly placed and canceled large orders on one side of the order book while executing trades on the other, with a cancellation-to-execution value ratio of roughly 30:1, generating about $119,000 in profits over three days. The activity primarily involved Brent crude perps. Solidus said the pattern resembled spoofing but acknowledged that manipulative intent remains unproven. Hyperliquid Labs emphasized that all orders, cancellations and trades are recorded on a transparent public blockchain and can be independently reviewed. — link
